title: Security posture discovery - Meridian Health
next_steps: Alex to share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/27001 summary via secure link
Samir to schedule architecture deep dive for private deployment options week of 11/24
Customer to provide retention requirements and list of regulated datasets by 11/25
action_items: Alex Chen - Share SOC2 attestation, ISO summary, network diagram - due 2025-11-24
Samir Patel - Set up technical deep dive (private deployment) and invite infra folks - due 2025-11-26
Alyssa Morgan - Send list of regulated datasets and retention windows - due 2025-11-25
summary: Initial security posture discovery focused on whether Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private meets Meridian Health's compliance needs. Main concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC granularity, audit logs retention and export, encryption at rest/in-transit and KMS integration, and data residency/retention policy. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, schedule architecture deep dive, customer to share dataset/retention requirements.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Samir our SE. Quick intros?
[00:08] Rachel Kim: Rachel Kim, CISO at Meridian Health. We're evaluating options for hosting patient-facing NLP features, so security is top of mind.
[00:15] Tom Ellis: Tom Ellis, VP Eng. I'll be coordinating infra.
[00:18] Alyssa Morgan: Alyssa, cloud architect. I'll own compliance mapping.
[00:22] Alex Chen: Great, appreciate that. Agenda — high level security posture, then dig into SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and retention. Happy to answer hosted vs dedicated vs private questions as we go.
[00:34] Samir Patel: Quick note, some of the product names might come out wrong in my head, I mean Redwood Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem) and our hosted API.
[00:42] Rachel Kim: That's fine. Our baseline: must be SOC 2 Type II and ideally ISO 27001. We also need SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning, and audit logs exported to our SIEM. Encryption keys must be customer-managed if possible.
[00:56] Alex Chen: Totally. We are SOC 2 Type II certified and we have an ISO summary — I'll share attestation docs. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via bring-your-own KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS and other HSM providers).
[01:12] Tom Ellis: For Private, do you mean full on-prem or VPC with private control plane?
[01:18] Samir Patel: We have both. Private (VPC) gives you a customer-managed VPC with a private control plane and optional on-prem package for air-gapped. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our infra with isolation and SLAs. Hosted is multi-tenant.
[01:32] Rachel Kim: We prefer VPC model for PHI — isolation plus ability to route logs into our Splunk. Can you stream audit logs in real time?
[01:41] Alex Chen: Yes, audit logs can be exported to S3, pushed via Kinesis, or forwarded to SIEMs; near real-time forwarding is supported. We also have immutable audit trails for admin actions.
[01:51] Alyssa Morgan: How granular is RBAC? Need ability to separate dev/test/prod, and limit model deploy permissions to a small group.
[01:58] Samir Patel: RBAC is role-based with custom roles; you can create roles that only allow model inference, others for deploy, and controls for rollout policies. There is SSO sync via SCIM so your identity provider can manage group membership.
[02:11] Tom Ellis: Does RBAC integrate with Okta groups? We'll want group sync.
[02:15] Alex Chen: Yes, Okta and Azure AD via SAML + SCIM are supported. There can be delays in group sync depending on IdP, but provisioning works.
[02:22] Rachel Kim: Data residency — we have patients in two regions, US and EU — do you support region pinning and EU-only storage?
[02:29] Samir Patel: We support region-aware deployments; for Private you can ensure data never leaves the customer's VPC. For Dedicated we have region pinning options; for Hosted we offer regional endpoints and contractual data residency controls for enterprise plans.
[02:42] Alyssa Morgan: For encryption keys, if we bring our own KMS, are logs encrypted with the same keys?
[02:49] Alex Chen: Data at rest is encrypted. User data blobs and model cache can be encrypted with your KMS; audit logs at rest in our storage can also be encrypted with customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted multi-tenant, we support CMEK for enterprise accounts — there are some limitations around third-party key lifecycle. We'll include details in the doc pack.
[03:10] Tom Ellis: Regulatory question: do you provide artifact retention and deletion workflows for subject requests (like patient data deletion)?
[03:17] Samir Patel: Yes, we provide policy-driven retention windows and deletion APIs; for Private you control retention. For Hosted we can set retention per-tenant and have deletions processed with attestations. There can be delays for cached tokens, we should map those.
[03:32] Rachel Kim: Audit logs retention — we need at least seven years for some flows. Is that feasible?
[03:37] Alex Chen: Seven years is long but supported if you export logs to your storage; we can retain within Redwood for shorter windows and advise exporting for long-term retention. We'll document recommended patterns and costs.
[03:48] Alyssa Morgan: On the security report, do you share pen test reports and scope?
[03:52] Alex Chen: We can share redacted pen test summaries and remediation plans; full reports go through an NDA for obvious reasons.
[03:58] Tom Ellis: Performance — if we go Private, what's the process for benchmarking model latency with our token sizes?
[04:05] Samir Patel: We can do a hosted benchmark or run tests in your VPC; typically SE runs a throughput/latency benchmark using a sample workload. We may ask for small dataset and expected prompt patterns. We'll also recommend quantization and batching config.
[04:20] Rachel Kim: Is there a formal SOC2/ISO audit contact? We need an audit letter and sometimes direct QnA.
[04:26] Alex Chen: Yes, our compliance team supports SOC2 exchanges and ISO summaries; we also provide an audit contact for enterprise contracts. I'll include contact details in the packet.
[04:34] Alyssa Morgan: Ok, a couple of nitty gritty: do you store KV cache or prefix cache that might include PII? How is that handled?
[04:43] Samir Patel: We do KV/prefix caching for inference performance. For Private and Dedicated you can configure cache policies to evict or not persist across sessions, and we can disable caching for sensitive flows. For Hosted we have configurable retention and the ability to opt-out of long-term cache storage. There are some tradeoffs with latency.
[05:00] Tom Ellis: You mentioned immutable admin audit trails — are those tamper-evident?
[05:04] Alex Chen: They're write-once in our storage layer with integrity checks; for Private you can mirror them into your own S3 for additional controls.
[05:12] Rachel Kim: Regarding SSO failover — if IdP is down, do you have emergency admin accounts? We need break-glass procedures.
[05:19] Samir Patel: We support emergency SAML bypass tokens and emergency local admin accounts with strict controls. We can tie that into your incident response playbook.
[05:28] Alyssa Morgan: For encryption, you mentioned HSMs; do you integrate with customer HSMs on-prem?
[05:34] Alex Chen: For Private on-prem installs, we can integrate with local HSMs; for cloud KMS we use provider-managed HSM-backed keys. We'll surface exact support matrix in the security pack.
[05:47] Tom Ellis: Cost question — if we require CMEK and long retention, is there a large delta in TCO?
[05:53] Samir Patel: Yes, both CMEK and long-term external storage add costs — CMEK adds key lifecycle/requests and Dedicated/Private has infra costs. We'll provide a TCO estimate in the follow-up.
[06:05] Rachel Kim: Any compliance gaps we should be aware of if we choose Hosted vs Private?
[06:09] Alex Chen: Hosted is fine for many regulated customers with contractual controls, but Private gives you maximum control for PHI and strict residency. We'll surface known limitations per mode in the doc.
[06:19] Tom Ellis: Can we get a sample service level agreement and incident response SLA?
[06:23] Alex Chen: Yes, sample SLA and IR runbooks will be included in the enterprise packet.
[06:28] Alyssa Morgan: Ok, sounds good. Let's walk through next steps.
[06:31] Alex Chen: Recap: we'll share SOC2/ISO docs, redacted pen test summary, network architecture diagram for Private and Dedicated, and a security FAQ. Samir will schedule a technical deep dive to run through deployment specifics and benchmarking. Meredith on our compliance team will be available for audit Qs.
[06:50] Rachel Kim: We'll send over dataset lists and retention requirements, and we'll review the packet once received. If anything looks good we'll schedule the deep dive next week.
[06:59] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll send the packet and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[07:05] (call ends)
